questiontext.text:
A ship is out at sea.

A lighthouse is on a bearing of {@bearhh@}\(^{\circ}\) from the ship.

A port is on a bearing of {@bearpp@}\(^{\circ}\) from the lighthouse.

The ship is {@ss@}km from the lighthouse, and the port is {@pp@}km from the lighthouse.

How far is the ship from the port?

Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

// point L var p4 = board.create('intersection', [l1, c1, 0], { name: 'L', size: 0.1, fixed: true, visible: true, strokeColor: '#901B77', fillColor: '#901B77', label: { fontSize: 15, autoPosition: true, offset: [-12.5, 20] } }); // ray var l2 = board.create('line', [p4, p6], { fixed: true, straightFirst: false, straightLast: true, strokeWidth: 2, visible: false }); // ----- Find point P ------- // circle from L of radius LP var c2 = board.create('circle', [p4, [p4.X() + {#float(pp/10)#}, p4.Y()]], { // feed in length LP here fixed: true, visible: false }); As the vertical dotted lines are parallel (North), the co-interior angle at L is \(180-{@bearhh@}={@180-bearhh@}\)

So, the angle inside the triangle at the lighthouse L is \(360-{@180-bearhh@}-{@bearpp@}={@tt@}\)

We have two sides and an angle inbetween, so we can use the cosine rule.

\(a^2=b^2+c^2-2bc\cos{A}\)

\(a^2={@ss@}^2+{@pp@}^2-2 \times {@ss@} \times {@pp@} \times \cos{{@tt@}}\)

\(a^2={@dispsf(squared,7)@}\)...

\(a=\sqrt{{@dispsf(squared,7)@}...}\)

\(a={@dispsf(exactside,5)@}\)...

\(a={@tans1@}\) km to 3 significant figures.
